title: HIRN congratulates Enrique Eduardo Sanchez Castro as the PanKbase DEPOSIT award winner
bodyHtml:
We are thrilled to announce that Enrique Eduardo Sanchez Castro has been selected as the PanKbase DEPOSIT award winner, as part of the HIRN Data Scholars Initiative. Enrique is currently a PhD candidate in the laboratory of Dr. Jeffrey Millman at Washington University in St. Louis.  

Enrique’s project aims to build a harmonized, metadata-rich, multiomic atlas of human stem cell-derived islet (SC-islet) differentiation, with the ultimate goal of fully integrating this resource into PanKbase. By unifying and standardizing diverse SC-islet datasets, his work will create a centralized, interoperable platform for the Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) research community to explore single-cell data from SC-islets.

This new resource is designed to enhance the reproducibility, accessibility, and overall value of existing datasets. By making high-quality, well-annotated data more widely available, Enrique’s project will help accelerate the development of more effective SC-islet differentiation strategies. In the long run, this work has the potential to drive progress toward improved diabetes therapies through regenerative medicine.

Please join us in congratulating Enrique on this well-deserved recognition, and stay tuned for more updates as his project progresses!
summary: Enrique Eduardo Sanchez Castro, a PhD candidate at Washington University in St. Louis, has been awarded the PanKbase DEPOSIT award through the HIRN Data Scholars Initiative for his project to build a harmonized, multiomic atlas of stem cell-derived islet differentiation, which will advance data accessibility and research in diabetes therapy.
